v0.20.4 — the exchange wallet, after an attack round: no paid withdrawal shown as failed, payments between customers credited

**Same chain, no coordinated update.** Replace the binary and restart; your data stays. Nothing in
this release changes consensus, the chain state or what nodes say to each other. Only the wallet
RPC (`server=1` in `helix.conf`) and `helix-cli` change — **anyone running the wallet RPC of
0.20.3 should update.**

**Wallet RPC (#265)**

- **A withdrawal that paid no longer shows as given up.** The wallet asked the node about a pending
  transaction and then about the sender's nonce, one after the other. When the block holding that
  very withdrawal landed between the two answers — the withdrawal had left this node's pool, and
  another validator included it — the wallet gave it up, and `gettransaction` showed
  `confirmations: -1` for good. An exchange that pays a withdrawal again when it reads -1 would
  have paid twice. Now a send is given up only after the wallet has read the block that used its
  nonce, and a block that holds a send the wallet gave up on settles it.
- **A withdrawal to another customer's deposit address is a `send` and a `receive`,** as Bitcoin
  Core lists a payment to the wallet's own address. 0.20.3 treated it as a sweep and listed no
  receive, so the receiving customer was never credited. A sweep is now only a move to the hot
  address.
- **Wrong passwords are slowed down as in Bitcoin Core:** each is answered after 250 ms, at most
  four at a time — sixteen guesses a second however many connections. The right password never
  waits.
- **A refused client cannot fill the log or the memory:** refusals and wrong passwords are one log
  line a minute with their count, and a request is read only once the address and the password are
  accepted.
- `helix-cli -version` prints the version (0.20.3 printed the usage and exited 1).

How an exchange or custodian puts this together: [Integrating
Helix](https://github.com/silvra-net/helix/blob/master/docs/exchange-integration.md).

**Helix is a testnet.** Its chain is reset when a release needs it, and HLX on it has no value.
